newsitem.title: DUBAI: Australian air stewardess appeals UAE jail term.
newsitem.headline: Australian air stewardess appeals UAE jail term.

text.p: An Australian air stewardess held in the United Arab Emirates on drugs charges since March has appealed against a four-year jail term imposed on her last month, an Australian diplomat said on Tuesday.
"Julia Alexander has appealed the prison sentence and we would offer her all the assistance she might need," John Yewdall, Australian Consul-General in Dubai, told Reuters.
The appeal will be heard on July 28.

"While we respect the law of the United Arab Emirates and the right of any country to apply its laws, we are concerned that we have one of our nationals in jail," he said, stressing there would be no intervention at government level.

Alexander, 25, was arrested in Dubai in March with two other people -- a Lebanese and a UAE national -- on charges of possessing Valium tablets and using marijuana. They were transferred to prison in neighbouring Sharjah emirate.
Yewdall said Alexander was sentenced to four years in jail for using marijuana. Sources familiar with the case said the unnmamed Lebanese received the same sentence.
Lebanese consular officials were not available for comment.
"The arrest was a joint operation between the Sharjah and Dubai police," Yewdall said, adding that the initial arrest warrant was issued by Sharjah, one of the UAE's seven emirates.

The daily Gulf News said Alexander admitted smoking marijuana three days before her arrest during a visit to Sri Lanka and said the Valium tablets were sleeping pills used because of irregularity of her working hours.
